title: Colours & Common Sizes
description: Describe everyday items by colour, size, and appearance with accurate English adjectives.
objectives: Name primary and common secondary colours fluently
Use basic size adjectives (big, small, heavy, light, long, short)
Apply the crucial rule of English adjective word order: Adjective before Noun (never inflected for plural)

vocabularyList.definition: Of a colour at the end of the visible spectrum, like blood or a ripe ruby.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: She bought a bright red coat.

vocabularyList.definition: Of a colour intermediate between green and violet, like a clear sky.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: The sky is clear and blue today.

vocabularyList.definition: Of the colour between blue and yellow, like fresh grass or emeralds.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: Pakistan's national flag is green and white.

vocabularyList.definition: Of the colour between green and orange, like ripe lemons.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: He highlighted the rule with a yellow marker.

vocabularyList.definition: Of the very darkest colour owing to the absence of light.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: He wore smart black shoes to the interview.

vocabularyList.definition: Of the colour of milk or fresh snow.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: The classroom has clean white walls.

vocabularyList.definition: Of considerable size or extent; large.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: They live in a big house with a garden.

vocabularyList.definition: Of a size that is less than normal or usual.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: He lives in a small apartment.

vocabularyList.definition: Of great weight; difficult to lift or move.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: This suitcase is too heavy for one person.
Modern laptops are very light to carry.

sections.title: Position and Invariance of English Adjectives
sections.content:
An **adjective** describes a noun. In English, adjectives follow two vital structural rules:

### 1. Position Before Noun or After 'To Be'
- **Before the noun**: *a red car*, *a big room*, *heavy boxes*.
- **After 'to be'**: *The car is red*, *The room is big*, *The boxes are heavy*.

### 2. English Adjectives NEVER Have Plural Forms
Unlike many languages, English adjectives never change for plural nouns! You say **big houses**, NEVER *'bigs houses'*.

callouts.title: Size Before Colour
callouts.text: When using both size and colour together, size normally comes first: **a big red ball**, **a small green apple**.

callouts.title: No Plural Suffix on Adjectives
callouts.text: Remember: nouns can be plural (*books*), but adjectives never can (*red books*, never *reds books*).

sections.title: Lesson Summary
sections.content: What you learned about colours, sizes, and adjectives:
summaryPoints: English adjectives are placed BEFORE nouns (a blue pen) or AFTER the verb to be (The pen is blue).
Adjectives NEVER change for singular vs plural (red books, not reds books).
Adjectives do not change for gender in English.
Natural descriptive order: Size before Colour (a big green apple).
Master common opposites: big/small, heavy/light, black/white, long/short.
